problem: Transformer VLN models either let all 36 panoramic views attend to each other, which is costly and mixes in noise from spatially distant views, or use only isolated candidate views, as in Recurrent VLN-BERT, which can crop or obscure objects the instruction refers to.
motivation: Objects mentioned in instructions are often partly visible or missing in a single candidate view, so the agent needs nearby context. Distant views are usually unrelated and act as noise. The paper aims for a balance between memory cost and information integration.
key_idea: Use each candidate view as a slot in a modified Slot Attention that queries the 36 panoramic views under a local 3x3 attention mask, so candidate features are restored with neighbouring context.
insight: Local context around candidate views helps, but the attention span matters. In the mask-shape ablation, 3x3 gives the best SPL on both seen (71.89) and unseen (57.13) splits, while wide horizontal spans (1x7, 3x7) hurt generalization by adding noise from distant views. Removing the mask gives 55.99 unseen SPL, and 3 slot iterations is the best setting (57.13, versus 56.02 with none). The module also converges faster (100K iterations versus 300K for the baseline).
method: Slot-attention over panorama: the K candidate views (image plus angle features) initialise the slots/queries. The 36 panoramic view features serve as keys and values, and the softmax is taken over slots so slots compete for views.

Angle-preserving updates: only the image-feature part (2048-d) is updated. Angle features (128-d) are kept fixed in queries and keys and are excluded from values. LayerNorm and DropFeat (dropout 0.7) apply to image features only.
Iterative refinement: 3 iterations, each with a GRU and MLP residual update. The final slots are added residually to the candidate image features, giving the enhanced candidate features V^.
Local attention mask: the 36 views form a 3x12 grid that is circular horizontally. Each candidate attends only to a 3x3 neighbourhood (2x3 at the top or bottom row).
Stop view feature: the 'stop' candidate uses a max-pooled feature over all 36 views.
Plug-in on Recurrent VLN-BERT: the enhanced candidate views go into the original cross-attention/self-attention action decoder with the recurrent state.

setting.backbone: Recurrent VLN-BERT with LSA module (trained; ResNet-152 Places365 pre-extracted features)
setting.training_data: R2R train plus PREVALENT augmented data, 100K iterations, batch size 8, one 2080Ti; initialisation and pre-training as in Recurrent VLN-BERT
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, pre-extracted ResNet-152 features) plus angle features
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic action space over candidate views)

numbers.evidence: Table 1 (results on R2R val and test splits), LSA row

numbers_note: Table 1 prints integer SR/SPL. The ablation tables give finer numbers (3x3 mask: val-seen SR 76.30 / SPL 71.89, val-unseen SR 62.49 / SPL 57.13); their column headers both read 'Val Unseen', but the first pair is evidently val-seen.
results: LSA reaches R2R test-unseen SR 64 and SPL 59, versus 63 and 57 for Recurrent VLN-BERT. It is strongest on val-seen (SR 76, SPL 72, versus 72 and 68) and matches the baseline on val-unseen SPL (57), with NE lowest on all splits. It uses 100K training iterations versus 300K for the baseline.
limitations: Gains on val-unseen are negligible (SR 62 versus 63, SPL 57 versus 57); most improvement is on seen environments.
Only R2R is evaluated, with pre-extracted global image features and no object features. Only the discrete setting is tested.
Slot count and mask shape are hand-tuned (3x3, 3 iterations) and the slots depend on the panoramic candidate structure.
